scope: Thirty completed GCP scalar judges requests: three exact GGUF artifacts, ten fixed prompt positions each. This is a local final-output rubric, not official competition judging, ARC-Easy accuracy or the composite ADTC score.
policy: Every original criterion label and weight is retained, but pass/fail decisions follow manual semantic review rather than keyword matching.

All full prompts, answer fields and reasoning_content fields were read. Only substantive student-facing final text earns points; separate reasoning_content and text within literal <think> blocks are excluded.
An unclosed <think> block yields no final text. An empty or non-substantive final receives zero on all criteria, including error-avoidance criteria.
A substantive final fragment after a closed think block may earn only the criteria actually completed before the 1,024-token cap; its partial status remains explicit.

Unresolved contradictions fail the affected criterion. A correct final expression may earn its separate criterion even where a separately scored derivation or verification criterion fails; conflicting supporting work remains flagged.
The existing concise-response threshold is at most 500 final-text characters. Exceeding one requested explanatory sentence is separately flagged, without introducing a new scoring threshold.

An analogy may convey a correct semantic relation without the exact scientific wording. A clearly false relation, such as proteins being instructions rather than products, fails the affected biological and analogy criteria.
A corrective follow-up must repair an incorrect conceptual answer; merely relabelling lack of understanding as incorrect and repeating a generic analogy is insufficient.
The repeated proportional-model prompt is retained at its two original positions; these ten positions contain nine unique prompt wordings.
Scores measure final delivery under this recorded protocol, not unbounded-budget capability. No Mac grades, response timings or memory measurements are pooled into this GCP assessment.

source_snapshot.scope: Exact captured prefix of a growing append-only JSONL file; individual record hashes exclude newline.

independent_review.scope: Full independent reading of control automated_01, automated_02, human_01, human_02, human_04, human_05 and LFM/Mini human_02; explicit root adjudication of Mini's corrective-follow-up criterion.
findings: Control scores 8, 1, 3, 6, 8 and 9 respectively on the six reviewed prompts. The inverse-effectiveness claim and incorrect 24.3% check remain explicit.
LFM's partial DNA final earns c1/c2/c3/c4 = 5; proteins-as-instructions fails c5/c6.
Mini's DNA final earns c1/c2/c3 = 4. Root confirms c8 fails: the supposed incorrect answer expresses only lack of understanding and the follow-up repairs no wrong conception.

prompts.title: Two Sigma proportional model

criteria.criterion: states direct proportionality R = kP
as personalization tends to zero the rate tends to zero
as personalization tends to infinity the linear rate is unbounded
defines the variables and positive proportionality constant
does not invent a square-root-of-two constant or Kahneman attribution

prompts.reason: States rate = k × personalization and explicitly gives both requested limits. The proportionality-constant criterion fails: positivity is unstated and the final claim that effectiveness varies inversely with personalization conflicts with its earlier constant definition. The numerical example P = 10 does not approximate an infinite limit; credit is based on the explicit final limit statements.

prompts.title: Mastery differential equation

criteria.criterion: gives S(t) = T + (S(0) - T)e^(-kt)
applies the initial condition
states convergence to T for positive k
connects the ceiling or rate to individual learning
relates one-to-one gains to the difficulty of scaling tutoring

prompts.reason: Correctly applies S(0) = S₀ to obtain C = −ln|T − S₀|. Later inversion changes the required e^(−kt) into e^(+kt), producing the wrong solution. The explanation incorrectly predicts decreasing mastery and misstates the Two Sigma problem; convergence, learning interpretation and scaling criteria fail.

prompts.title: Offline LLM capacity

criteria.criterion: recognizes that parameter count is underdetermined
computes the 200 ms operation budget as 8 × 10^11
requires an output-length assumption
requires operations per parameter per generated token
does not treat two tokens per character as enough to size the model

prompts.reason: Conflates operations, characters, tokens and model parameters, concluding that the maximum model size is 0.8 tokens. It neither identifies underdetermination nor computes the operation budget or the required per-parameter/per-token workload.

prompts.title: Lagos chalk calculation

criteria.criterion: selects option C
gives ₦3,000
keeps the requested answer concise

prompts.reason: The delivered answer is B, ₦2,500, not C, ₦3,000, and no calculation is shown. It earns only the independent two-point concise-response criterion.

prompts.title: Photosynthesis multiple choice

criteria.criterion: selects option B
identifies photosynthesis
explains conversion of light into stored chemical energy or food
keeps the requested explanation concise

prompts.reason: Selects B and correctly describes sunlight-driven conversion of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. The final is within the established 500-character concise bound, though it exceeds one explanatory sentence.

prompts.title: Average-speed misconception

criteria.criterion: gives 53.3 km/h
computes 1.5 h, 0.75 h, and 2.25 h
uses total distance divided by total time
explains why the arithmetic mean fails for equal distances
includes an intuitive second example
teaches a future recognition rule

prompts.reason: States total distance / total time and teaches that rule for future use. The main calculation incorrectly adds 1.5 h and 0.75 h to 2 h and concludes 60 km/h; it does not explain unequal time weighting. The separate 60 m in one minute plus 60 m in two minutes example correctly gives 120 m in three minutes, earning the example criterion despite not explicitly evaluating the quotient.

prompts.title: DNA genes chromosomes and proteins

criteria.criterion: identifies the misconception that the terms are not synonyms
describes DNA as genetic information or material
defines a gene as a segment of DNA
states that chromosomes package DNA
connects gene expression to proteins
uses a simple analogy without a flagged scientific error
asks a check question
provides a response for an incorrect student answer

prompts.reason: DNA contains instructions, genes are individual recipes within that DNA book, and chromosome/protein containers organize those recipes. The storage analogy and relationship check are usable. It does not explicitly identify the synonym misconception or connect gene expression to protein products; the follow-up is for an understanding student or generic continuing confusion, not an incorrect answer.

prompts.title: Bilingual photosynthesis tutoring

criteria.criterion: includes all six required scientific terms
correctly states the inputs and outputs
states that chlorophyll absorbs or captures light
contains a substantive Yorùbá explanation
uses a West African everyday example
ends with English and Yorùbá understanding questions

prompts.reason: The English explanation omits water and chlorophyll. The section labelled Yorùbá repeats English verbatim, and the quiz text does not supply substantive Yorùbá translations or understanding questions. No locally grounded West African example is delivered.

prompts.title: Two Sigma model repeat

criteria.criterion: states direct proportionality R = kP
as personalization tends to zero the rate tends to zero
as personalization tends to infinity the linear rate is unbounded
defines the variables and positive proportionality constant
does not invent a square-root-of-two constant or Kahneman attribution

prompts.reason: Defines L = kP and the learning-rate/personalization variables, then correctly states both limits. It never establishes k > 0, so the complete positive-constant criterion is not met; no fabricated square-root constant or attribution is introduced.

prompts.title: Onitsha rice profit

criteria.criterion: computes total cost as ₦74,000
identifies 15 kg remaining
reduces the price to ₦1,955 per kg
computes batch revenues ₦57,500 and ₦29,325
computes total revenue as ₦86,825
computes profit as ₦12,825
computes percentage profit as 17.3%
checks by a genuinely different method

prompts.reason: The main calculation and final answers correctly give ₦86,825 revenue, ₦12,825 profit and 17.3%. The proposed check incorrectly applies the full-price margin to all 40 kg, giving ₦18,000 and 24.3%; it fails the separate verification criterion and leaves conflicting supporting arithmetic.

observations: All ten final responses finish, but chalk, the ODE solution and average-speed answer are incorrect.
The main rice result is correct; its independent check is wrong. The correct final answer does not make the verification valid.
The two identical proportional-model prompts return different text, though both receive 8 points under the fixed rubric.
